entities.name: Macropedius
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Georgius Macropedius (1487-1558), born Joris van Lanckvelt in Gemert, Brabant, was a preeminent Dutch humanist, schoolmaster, and arguably the greatest Latin playwright of the 16th century. Adopting his Hellenized name ('long-footed') upon joining the Brethren of the Common Life, Macropedius dedicated his life to education and literary production, profoundly influencing educational curricula and theatrical development across Northern Europe during the Reformation and Counter-Reformation. His significance lies in his masterful adaptation of classical dramatic forms to address contemporary moral and pedagogical concerns, making complex humanist ideals accessible to a wider audience, particularly students.

Macropedius's most celebrated work, *Hecastus* (1538), a Dutch adaptation of the medieval morality play *Everyman*, achieved immense popularity, seeing multiple editions and translations into German, Danish, and Dutch. This play, alongside others such as *Asotus* (1537), *Petriscus* (1537), and *Andrisca* (1538), served not merely as entertainment but as a crucial pedagogical tool, designed to instruct students in rhetoric, Latin, and ethics. As rector of schools in 's-Hertogenbosch, Liège, and Utrecht, he implemented these plays as integral components of the curriculum, fostering a vibrant student theater culture that trained generations in humanist thought and expression, often featuring allegorical figures and moral dilemmas reflecting the intellectual and religious ferment of the era.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Macropedius was a pivotal figure in Northern European humanism, whose Latin plays were integral to 16th-century education, influencing generations of students and shaping the development of school drama as a genre.
